subject: Post-call: Competitive throughput & latency workbook + execution asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Mercer <evan.mercer@acmecorp.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Competitive throughput & latency workbook + execution asks

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great discussion. This thread captures the immediate follow-ups and the concrete lab asks so we can run an apples-to-apples comparison between Redwood and the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned. Please skim and confirm availability for a 48-hour test window next week.

Summary of goals
- Objective: quantify p95 and p99 latency and steady-state tokens/sec across typical request mixes for Acme search + summarization flows.
- Outcome: a short results sheet (p95/p99, median, tokens/sec, throughput at 95% utilization), and a decision recommendation for the next procurement step.

Proposed tests (workbook attached — redwood-compare-workbook-v1.xlsx)
1) Baseline single-concurrency latency sweep
   - Models: Redwood-optimized open model (quantized), Hyperscaler API v3 baseline (float32)
   - Payloads: 3 buckets (query=18 tokens, short context=120 tokens, long context=800 tokens)
   - Measure: cold vs warm p50/p95/p99, mean token/sec for a 10-minute sustained run

2) Throughput/concurrency ramp (tokens/sec stability)
   - Ramp from 1 to 128 concurrent streams; record p95/p99 and token consumption
   - Track queueing effects and GPU memory pressure; capture KV cache hit rate where available

3) A/B response-quality sanity check
   - 50 random prompts from your production set (see sample-prompts.jsonl)
   - Check for divergence (top-line metrics only) so we can validate no major correctness regressions when using quantized variants

Instrumentation & deliverables
- Please provide a test service account and a minimal token-mix file (example attached: acme-internal-token-mix.txt) so we can mirror request distribution.
- Deliverables: raw run logs, CSV summary (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failed requests), and a short one-page recommendation.
- Lab owner: Redwood (Marissa / Dev) will run tests; Acme to provide access and approval for the scheduled window.

Constraints you mentioned on the call
- Cannot run tests during business hours due to internal rate limits (preferred window: 02:00–06:00 PT).
- Hyperscaler quota is limited to 250 concurrent requests per project.

Next steps (action items)
- Evan/Priya: confirm the test window (2–4 hour blocks overnight) and provide a service account by EOD Monday.
- Acme: confirm which Hyperscaler model version you want us to include (you mentioned HS-Gen2-v1).
- Redwood: we will provision the test harness and share a short runbook by Monday morning.

Attachments: redwood-compare-workbook-v1.xlsx, sample-prompts.jsonl, acme-internal-token-mix.txt

Thanks — I’ll block a short (15–20m) sync after the first run to go over anomalies.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Evan Mercer <evan.mercer@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 06:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive throughput & latency workbook + execution asks

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan and workbook. Priya and I reviewed internally, and we can do an overnight test window Wednesday night (May 27) from 02:30–05:30 PT. Couple of notes from our infra/ops side: 

- Hyperscaler model: please include HS-Gen2-v1 and HS-Gen2-quant-lite (we want to see both float and their quantized offering if you can).
- Quota: we can bump to 350 concurrent for that window but need at least 24-hour notice.
- Dataset access: I’ll create a service account and drop the key into the shared Drive link you listed. Expect that by EOD Monday.

Two asks from Acme: 
1) Don’t run tests that write to our production indexes — read-only queries only.
2) If you see p99 spikes > 2s, capture a full request/response pair and mark it P0 for follow-up.

We’re good to proceed on the runbook schedule. Quick Q: will Redwood include both quantized and non-quantized execution traces (so we can see token/sec differences)?

Appreciate it — Evan

Evan Mercer
Principal SRE, Acme Corp
ev an.mercer@acmecorp.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Competitive throughput & latency workbook + execution asks

Forwarding Evan’s confirmation — proposed execution plan below for the lab team.

Lab runbook (high level)
- Prep (Mon/Tue)
  - Validate sample-prompts.jsonl tokenization and build three payload buckets via our harness generator.
  - Confirm Hyperscaler endpoints and API keys (from Evan).
  - Configure datadog spans: redwood.request.latency, redwood.kv_cache.hits, redwood.tokens.per_sec; add hyperscaler.* prefixed metrics for comparison.

- Run (Wed 02:30–05:30 PT) — three phases
  1) Warmup: 15 mins low qps to prime caches
  2) Latency sweep: single-stream p95/p99 captures across payloads (repeat x3)
  3) Ramp to 128 concurrent (or until quota limit); maintain each step for 6 minutes to capture steady-state

- Data capture
  - Export per-request latency with request-size / model / concurrency tags
  - Compute tokens/sec from output length and requests/sec; store CSVs in Drive under /ACME/compare/results/20260527

Acceptance criteria for run validity
  - No more than 2% 5xx on any sustained phase
  - Stable tokens/sec (variance < 12%) for the 6-min steady windows

Post-run analysis plan
  - Produce a single-page summary (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, failed%) and a short appendix with raw CSVs and a short quality-check for the 50 prompts.

Jonas — can you validate we have the instrumentation hooks for token/sec and kv cache metrics? Also, please pre-seed the quantized variant on the test instance so warmup times are meaningful.

I’ll update the workbook with the exact command lines and the Drive path once Evan uploads the service account.

—
Dev Patel
Infra & Performance, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
